result.rationale: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy` with no nil check, so deleting a stale/unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404. The client delete action also calls destroyRecord without a .catch (unlike save's .catch(popupAjaxError)), so the error silently disappears. Mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: destroy calls host.destroy on the unchecked result of EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, so deleting an unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404. A double-delete from the UI (the trash button has no in-flight guard, so a second confirm fires a second DELETE) or a stale id from another tab produces a 500 that, combined with the missing .catch in the client, disappears with no error shown to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately calls `host.destroy` without nil-checking. If the id is unknown/already deleted, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` and return a 500 instead of a controlled 404/422. On the client, the trash button (`embeddable-host.hbs`) has no disabled/in-flight guard and the `delete()` action calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch(...)`, so repeated/stale deletes can silently fail, aligning with the finding.
